title: Minecraft's First New Dimension in 15 Years Comes With Blue Bunnies
summary:
Fifteen years. That's how long Minecraft fans have waited for a brand-new dimension. At Minecraft Live, Mojang finally announced one: The Sift. The last new realm was The End, which arrived in 2011. Since then? Nothing. So this is a huge deal for players who have explored every corner of the Overworld and the Nether.

The Sift will appear first in Minecraft Dungeons II, the sequel to the well-loved co-op dungeon crawler, which launches September 29. The main Minecraft game won't get The Sift until next year. What's actually inside it? Not much detail yet — except that it will feature blue bunnies. That's the one confirmed creature so far, and the internet is already obsessed.

Dungeons II itself is getting some big upgrades. There's a brighter new art style, a story built around the Deep Dark and Ancient Cities (yes, the Warden is involved), and — finally — the ability to jump. Armor now comes in four pieces like the main game, plus talismans that give passive abilities. Levels are bigger and interconnected, so you choose your own route instead of picking missions off a map.

Meanwhile, underground ice caves are coming to the base game. These rare "cold biomes" are packed with ore and glowing ice crystals that work as a light source. A new mob, the frozen zombie, lobs ice balls at you. Get hit enough times and you freeze solid. The good news? You can throw the ice balls right back — at the zombie, or at your friends.

Also announced: Minecraft arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 on October 27, with upgraded graphics. Not a bad year to be a block person.
why_it_matters: It shows how a game can stay alive for well over a decade by rationing its biggest surprises, and how studios increasingly use cheaper spin-offs as testing grounds for features that later reach the main product — a pattern you can see far beyond gaming, in apps and phones too.

background_read: Minecraft is a 'sandbox' game — instead of following one story, players build, mine, and explore freely — and until now it has had only three dimensions: the Overworld where you start, the Nether (a hot, dangerous underworld), and The End (a dark void where the Ender Dragon boss lives).
It is made by Mojang, a Swedish studio that Microsoft now owns; Mojang also makes spin-offs such as Minecraft Dungeons, a co-op game in which friends fight through levels together.
Spin-offs often get new ideas first, because they are smaller and cheaper to change — features that players love can later be moved into the main game.
Minecraft Live, where The Sift was announced, is Mojang's yearly livestreamed show, the moment when the studio reveals everything it has planned for the coming year.
New dimensions are the biggest kind of update a game like this can receive, because they need brand-new land, creatures, and travel rules built from scratch.

perspectives.description: Dungeons II fans get The Sift first, plus jumping, talismans, four-piece armor, and bigger interconnected levels. For them the spin-off stops looking like a side project and starts looking like the main event.

People who have explored every corner of the Overworld and Nether are told to wait yet another year while a spin-off gets the headline feature. The announcement also gives very little detail about The Sift itself, which makes the hype feel thin.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral — analysts of how games are built
perspectives.description: Dimension-sized updates are the most expensive kind of content, so studios release them where risk is lowest and feedback is fastest. Historically, spin-offs and beta versions have worked as test kitchens before ideas land in the main game.

The blue bunnies are clearly a teaser meant to keep speculation running until the main-game release. Watch whether the ice caves, frozen zombie, and Switch 2 launch arrive on schedule — and whether Dungeons II players end up testing The Sift for everyone else.
